description: Smoothest large body in the solar system — no mountain on Europa rises higher than a few hundred metres. Beneath its 20-km ice crust lies a global salt-water ocean ~100 km deep, holding more than twice the water in all of Earth's oceans combined. Tidal flexing from Jupiter keeps that ocean liquid and chemically active; magnetic-field signatures and Hubble observations of plumes suggest material from the subsurface ocean reaches the surface periodically. NASA's Europa Clipper (en route) and ESA's JUICE will both scrutinise the ice shell and ocean dynamics through the early 2030s.
surface_composition: Water-ice crust ~15–25 km thick, fractured by chaos terrain into a network of arcuate ridges and lenticulae; salts (likely magnesium sulfate + sodium chloride) tint the ice red-brown in the chaos regions.
